subject: Clarifying BYOK entitlements & dataflow for Private deployment onboarding
messages:
From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@medsys-health.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: complianceteam@medsys-health.com
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — BYOK entitlements question

Hi Laura / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from our security team: 1) Under the proposed DPA annex, will Redwood have any ability to export customer CMKs (even temporarily) for forensic work or disaster recovery? 2) Can you confirm which operator roles (if any) in the private deployment will be able to access unencrypted token-level telemetry?

We want to map this against our internal risk matrix before the procurement review next Tuesday.

Attaching the MedSys template for BYOK handoff to show the fields we usually require.

Thanks,
Jacob
Jacob Lee
Head of Security Integrations — MedSys Health
jacob.lee@medsys-health.com
(415) 555-0198

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@medsys-health.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — BYOK entitlements question

Jacob —

Short answers up front: Redwood will NOT export customer CMKs. Customer keys remain in your KMS (BYOK) and we only receive a wrapped key material reference for provisioning; there is no transfer of plaintext CMK. Operator roles cannot decrypt customer application data or token-level plaintext.

More context below and a proposed clause we can include in the DPA annex.

-- On Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 09:12 AM Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@medsys-health.com> wrote:
> Hi Laura / Kimberly,
>
> Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from our security team: 1) Under the proposed DPA annex, will Redwood have any ability to export customer CMKs (even temporarily) for forensic work or disaster recovery? 2) Can you confirm which operator roles (if any) in the private deployment will be able to access unencrypted token-level telemetry?
>
> We want to map this against our internal risk matrix before the procurement review next Tuesday.
>
> Thanks,
> Jacob

Proposal (summary):
- Key custody: Customer retains sole control of CMKs in their KMS. Redwood will store a key reference and encrypted key material only if customer opts into an escrow workflow; escrow requires a separate signed addendum and notarized escrow key transfer.
- Export prohibition: Add explicit export prohibition language: "Redwood and its subprocessors shall not exfiltrate or export customer-controlled CMKs under any operational or legal contingency, unless a court order directed at the customer requires it and Customer provides prior written consent for a Redwood-defined narrow exception."
- Operator entitlements: Minimum operator set (tiered) — "On-call Support" (read-only orchestration logs, redacted telemetry), "Platform Engineers" (can request debug snapshots; any snapshot with token-level content requires customer approval and is delivered encrypted to the customer), "Escalation Forensics" (requires two-person approval from customer-designated approvers).

Attachments I am sending: RDW_DPA_BYOK_matrix_v1.pdf (summary clause language) and BYOK_handshake_matrix.xlsx (operational steps).

Let me know if you want this converted into tracked-redline language for your legal team. Happy to put Kimberly or Karthik on a call with your compliance radars.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@medsys-health.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: complianceteam@medsys-health.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — BYOK entitlements question

Laura —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft language. A couple of clarifications from our side before we bring this internally: 1) The escrow path is acceptable but we need a clearer definition of the "notarized escrow key transfer" process — who holds the notarization evidence and who can trigger a release? 2) For operator entitlements, can you commit to a technical control that ensures any debug snapshot containing token-level content is only delivered to the customer's KMS-wrapped container? We need proof-of-transport and proof-of-rotation artifacts for our auditors.

If useful, our compliance lead (complianceteam@medsys-health.com) can provide a short checklist of evidence types. We're trying to avoid open-ended clauses that leave interpretation to operations.

Jacob

> > Short answers up front: Redwood will NOT export customer CMKs. Customer keys remain in your KMS (BYOK) and we only receive a wrapped key material reference for provisioning; there is no transfer of plaintext CMK. Operator roles cannot decrypt customer application data or token-level plaintext.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@medsys-health.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — BYOK entitlements question

Jacob / MedSys compliance team —

Appreciate the specificity. A couple of operational commitments Redwood can add into the onboarding playbook and DPA annex that address your auditor checklist requests: 

1) Notarized escrow process: If escrow is selected, Redwood will use a 3rd-party key escrow custodian (named in the annex) and provide both parties with notarized transfer receipts. Release requires a customer-specified trigger (e.g., certified disaster recovery declaration) plus a Redwood internal approval plus custodial release proof. All release events are logged and the notarized evidence stored in the customer's drive folder and Redwood's encrypted audit logs.

2) Proof-of-transport: Any debug snapshot that contains tokens or PII will be encapsulated in a KMS-wrapped container bound to the customer's CMK. Redwood will publish a transport manifest (SHA256) and a signed rotation record whenever we ship a snapshot to the customer KMS.

3) Subprocessors: For Private deployments, Redwood limits operator subprocessors to three named entities (cloud infra partner for host provisioning, audited network provider, and a support tooling vendor). We will include a subprocessor addendum with a 30-day notice for changes and offer MedSys the right to object within 14 days.

4) Audit evidence bundle: At onboarding completion we will deliver an "evidence bundle" (logs, manifests, notarized receipts) over your secure drive link and a signed manifest with verifiable checksums.

If that meets your checklist we can draft the exact annex language and attach to the DocuSign flow. Otherwise flag the gaps and we will iterate.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
